summary: Throughput regression after optimizer config change — request stepwise rollback & validation checklist
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden ~30% throughput drop and increased queue latency after applying an optimizer profile "opt-v2-conservative" (auto-batching + conservative KV cache TTL + new quantization profile) during a scheduled maintenance. Impact: production traffic for VendrAI (dedicated pool) sees elevated tail latency and throttled throughput; some jobs timing out.

Impact:
- Elevated p95/p99 token latency across chat and batch generation routes.
- Throughput down ~25-35% versus baseline for the last 12 hours.
- No 5xx errors observed, but requests are queuing and some client timeouts reported.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: vendrai-dedicated-pool-us-east
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: gpt-4o-mini (chat), redwood/llama-2-13b-quant (batch embeddings)
- Changes applied: optimizer profile "opt-v2-conservative" pushed at 2026-03-09 02:15 UTC via Redwood Console rollout (canary -> global).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Send sustained load pattern from VendrAI production env using internal load generator (spike to 800 RPS sustained).
2. Observe queue length on console and increase in per-request latency.

Observed behavior:
- Continuous queuing visible on Redwood Console per-route dashboard.
- Autoscaler shows increased GPU utilization but fewer completed tokens/sec.
- SRE logs show increased kernel-level mem pressure on a subset of nodes.

Expected behavior:
- Comparable throughput to pre-change profile with reduced token-cost per request but without spike in tail latency.

Recent changes noted by customer:
- Applied new optimizer profile that lowered batch_max_size, enabled aggressive KV cache eviction TTL=30s, and switched to quant profile q4_0 (new experimental profile).

Logs (redacted):
- serving-runtime WARN: batch_flush_interval increased under mem pressure
- scheduler INFO: fallback to baseline model variant not triggered
- node-23 kernel: Dropping pagecache due to memory pressure (OOM avoid)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Initial triage: confirmed throughput drop correlated with config rollout window.
Checked rollout history: opt-v2-conservative applied as canary at 2026-03-09 01:45 UTC then promoted globally at 02:15 UTC.
Console traces show batch sizes reduced to median 8 from baseline 16; CPU/GPU imbalance observed on quantized model paths.
KV cache hit-rate dropped from 78% to 12% after TTL change, resulting in increased repeated prefix decoding workloads.
Memory pressure observed on 4/24 nodes serving quantized model; kernels report increased page cache churn.
No sign of request-level 5xx; customer timeouts appear client-side after exceeding application-level waiting threshold.

Hypothesis: combination of aggressive KV TTL + smaller batch target increased per-request compute and IO, exposing quant profile memory behavior; autoscaler reacting slowly due to GPU saturation on a few nodes.
Action taken: collected heap/tracemalloc on two affected nodes and requested SRE to run kernel VMstat sampling during load window.
Requested customer to switch a small portion of traffic to fallback model variant while we validate rollback path (partial traffic shift recommended).
Related logs/metrics attached to ticket (console links in related_confluence_pages).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 10:03 UTC: Thanks for reporting, VendrAI. We are triaging and will validate a safe rollback path. Can you confirm whether you have a pinned model variant or rely on automatic fallback?
VendrAI (Customer) 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC: We do not pin variants; we accepted the global rollout. We can route 10% of traffic to a pinned earlier variant if you provide instructions.

Samantha Li (SRE) 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC: Initial findings: KV cache hit-rate collapse is the primary suspect. Suggest rolling back TTL to previous value (300s) on canary subset and monitor p95/p99. Preparing rollback checklist.

Marco Reynolds (Eng - Optimize) 2026-03-10 12:02 UTC: Quant profile q4_0 is relatively new; observed higher memory working set in internal perf tests. Recommend fallback to q4_1 (safer) for affected model while investigating q4_0 behavior.

Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC: VendrAI approved a staged rollback (canary first). Scheduling rollback at 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC with monitoring window. Customer requested documented validation steps and rollback checklist.
VendrAI (Customer) 2026-03-10 13:05 UTC: Confirmed. Also asking for guidance on how to safely test optimizer changes in future without global impact.
resolution: Planned staged rollback executed for canary subset and then global rollback to previous optimizer profile 'opt-v1-stable' and quant profile q4_1. Rollout steps: 1) Set KV cache TTL back to 300s for 10% canary; 2) Revert batch_max_size to 16 for same canary; 3) Switch quant profile to q4_1 for canary; 4) Monitor 30-minute observation window for p95/p99 and throughput; 5) If metrics stable, promote to 100% in 3 waves. After canary success, promoted globally at 2026-03-10 15:05 UTC. Post-rollback metrics returned to baseline within 45 minutes.
workaround: For immediate mitigation prior to full rollback: 1) Route 20% of traffic to pinned variant pre-change via console routing rules. 2) Increase autoscaler aggressiveness (scale out threshold to 60% GPU util) for dedicated pool to absorb transient load. 3) Temporarily raise client-side request timeout to reduce perceived errors.
follow_up_actions: Action: Create a pre-rollout checklist in Confluence for optimizer changes (owner: Optimize team) - due 2026-03-20.
Action: Add automated KV cache TTL canary tests to Redwood Optimize (owner: Serving Reliability) - due 2026-04-01.
Action: Mark q4_0 as experimental in model catalog and disable global auto-promotion until additional perf tests pass (owner: Model Onboarding) - due 2026-03-18.
Action: Share post-rollback notes with VendrAI and run a joint validation window next deployment (owner: Support/SE) - scheduled 2026-03-16.
Action: Update Redwood Console with a one-click 'revert optimizer profile' button for dedicated pools (design brief created) - owner: Console UX, due 2026-04-15.
